newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU monetary panel meets on EMU budget pact.
newsitem.headline: EU monetary panel meets on EMU budget pact.

text.p: The European Union's (EU) monetary committee began a meeting on Tuesday to resolve outstanding issues on a budget disciplinary pact for countries joining a common currency.

EU monetary sources said the meeting of treasury and central bank officials is unlikely to make much progress, an impression confirmed by Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke on Monday.

Clarke told the British parliament that a progress report on the state of negotiations over economic and monetary union (EMU) would likely be put together by finance ministers next week for EU leaders to consider in Dublin on December 13 and 14.
"What I am anticipating as the most likely thing to come from ECOFIN is a report to go ahead to the summit at Dublin on where we are on discussions on all these things (concerning EMU)," Clarke said.
Officials said such a report would highlight not only the progress made but the differences EU governments still have over several important aspects to a budget stability pact.

Lack of an accord has been due largely to German demands for a much tougher pact, one that includes a quantitative definition of the economic circumstances under which a country inside EMU could avoid sanctions.
Under the plan, governments running deficits above three percent of total output could face stiff fines if they failed to curb expenditure.
The results of Tuesday's monetary committee gathering will form the basis for the drafting of a progress report by EU finance ministers on December 2.
